activity.notes: Devapala succeeded Dharmapala as a major Pala ruler. Pala inscriptions normally use regnal years without a securely fixed era, and modern reconstructions differ substantially. ATLAS therefore uses the conventional c.810–c.850 CE bracket while explicitly marking both boundaries approximate rather than presenting one reconstruction as exact.

sources.title: Everyday Life in the Pala Empire — Asiatic Society of Pakistan Publication No. 23
sources.citation_text: The historical study notes that a Devapala copper-plate is dated to his 35th or 39th regnal year and places his long reign approximately between 810 and 850 CE.

sources.title: Somapura Mahavihara — Banglapedia
sources.citation_text: Banglapedia identifies Devapala as Dharmapala's successor in the Pala dynasty and discusses building activity during his reign.
